messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Adderall is a central nervous system stimulant.
Adderall is used to treat attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
Adderall is used to treat a sleep disorder called narcolepsy.
Adderall contains mixed amphetamine and dextroamphetamine salts.
Adderall contains a combination of amphetamine and dextroamphetamine.
These substances affect chemicals in the brain and nerves.
These chemicals contribute to hyperactivity and impulse control.
For ADHD, Adderall is used in children 3 to 17 years of age and in adults.
Adderall may help increase attention and decrease impulsiveness and hyperactivity.
For narcolepsy, Adderall is used in people 6 years and older.
It is not known if Adderall is safe and effective for ADHD in children under 3 years of age.
It is not known if Adderall is safe and effective for narcolepsy in children under 6 years of age.
Adderall is a federally controlled substance (CII).
Adderall contains amphetamine.
Amphetamine can be a target for people who abuse prescription medicines or street drugs.
Keep Adderall in a safe place to protect Adderall from theft.
Triplet: ["amphetamine", "can be targeted by", "people who abuse prescription medicines or street drugs"]

The relation 'can be targeted by' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject substance is a potential object of misuse or abuse by the group specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has controlled substance schedule': The subject drug is classified under the controlled substance schedule specified by the object entity.
B. 'has warning': The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
C. 'has side effect': The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
D. 'interacts with': The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
E. 'has overdose symptom': An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
